title: Certified Kubernetes Application Developer (CKAD) Workloads & Patterns
summary: Master CKAD core competencies: multi-container Pod patterns (InitContainers, Sidecars, Adapters), container lifecycle health probes (liveness, readiness, startup), batch Jobs, and scheduled CronJobs.
learningObjectives: Design and deploy resilient multi-container Pods utilizing InitContainers for sequential startup gating and Sidecars for log shipping and processing.
Implement robust container health probes including HTTP GET, TCP Socket, and Exec liveness, readiness, and startup checks with realistic thresholds.
Orchestrate batch workloads and recurring automations with Kubernetes Jobs and CronJobs, configuring backoff limits, active deadlines, and concurrency policies.

curriculumModules.title: Multi-Container Pod Patterns: InitContainers, Sidecars, Adapters & Ambassadors
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: Pods encapsulate tightly coupled containers sharing network, IPC, and volume storage namespaces. InitContainers run to completion sequentially before application containers start. Sidecars run concurrently alongside main containers to handle logging, telemetry, caching, or proxying.
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Use shared emptyDir volumes for inter-container data exchange, set container-level resource limits, and utilize native Kubernetes 1.28+ built-in sidecar containers (restartPolicy: Always in initContainers) for deterministic startup and teardown ordering.

curriculumModules.title: Container Health Probes: Startup, Liveness, and Readiness Lifecycle Management
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: The Kubelet monitors container health via probes. Startup probes protect slow-starting applications by delaying liveness checks. Liveness probes detect deadlocks and trigger automated container restarts. Readiness probes govern whether a Pod receives traffic from backing Services.
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Decouple liveness checks from external downstream dependencies to prevent cascading restart storms across the cluster; only probe lightweight internal endpoints for liveness, and verify network dependencies in readiness probes.

curriculumModules.title: Batch & Scheduled Processing: Jobs, CronJobs, Deadlines & Concurrency
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: Jobs coordinate batch computation, running Pods to successful completion (exit code 0) with configurable completions, parallelism, and backoffLimits. CronJobs automate time-scheduled executions via cron syntax with concurrencyPolicies (Allow, Forbid, Replace).
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Always specify activeDeadlineSeconds and backoffLimit on Jobs to prevent runaway zombie pods and unbounded retries consuming cluster compute quotas.

labs.title: Multi-Container Pod Patterns: InitContainer Preconditions & Log-Processing Sidecars
labs.scenario: Configure an order processing microservice in namespace ecommerce requiring data preparation before the core application starts, alongside a log-processing sidecar container streaming events to a shared volume.
labs.productionContext: Enterprise production workloads frequently separate cross-cutting concerns (data pre-fetching, log aggregation, TLS termination) into distinct helper containers within the same Pod boundary.
objectives: Create namespace ecommerce for isolated commerce workloads

Add primary container app and sidecar container log-shipper mounted to the shared volume
Apply Pod manifest and verify Running phase in namespace ecommerce

labs.title: Container Health Probes & Scheduled Batch Automations
labs.scenario: Deploy an inventory management API with HTTP liveness and readiness health checks, and configure a scheduled inventory synchronization CronJob executing every 5 minutes in namespace logistics.
labs.productionContext: Production Kubernetes services rely on health probes for automatic healing and traffic gating, paired with CronJobs for scheduled data synchronization and periodic maintenance tasks.
objectives: Create namespace logistics for inventory workloads
Deploy inventory-api with HTTP liveness and readiness health probes
Schedule recurring CronJob inventory-sync executing every 5 minutes
Execute a one-off batch Job inventory-manual-sync to verify immediate execution

steps.title: Create Logistics Namespace
steps.instruction: Create namespace `logistics` using `kubectl create namespace logistics`.

steps.title: Author Deployment Manifest with Probes
steps.instruction: Create `/home/learner/inventory-api.yaml` with liveness probe on `/healthz` and readiness probe on `/ready`.

steps.title: Deploy API Workload
steps.instruction: Apply the Deployment manifest using `kubectl apply -f /home/learner/inventory-api.yaml`.

steps.title: Create Scheduled CronJob
steps.instruction: Create CronJob `inventory-sync` scheduled every 5 minutes in `logistics`.

steps.title: Create One-Off Batch Job
steps.instruction: Execute an immediate batch job `inventory-manual-sync` in `logistics`.

solutionCommands:
echo -e "apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: inventory-api
  namespace: logistics
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: inventory-api
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: inventory-api
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: inventory-api
        image: nginx:1.27-alpine
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 80
          initialDelaySeconds: 5
          periodSeconds: 10
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /ready
            port: 80
          initialDelaySeconds: 2
          periodSeconds: 5" > /home/learner/inventory-api.yaml
labs.troubleshootingGuide: Ensure namespace logistics exists, apply deployment with liveness and readiness probes, and create CronJob inventory-sync and Job inventory-manual-sync.

assessmentQuestions.question: What is the primary behavioral difference between a failed livenessProbe versus a failed readinessProbe?
options: (Recommended) A failed livenessProbe causes kubelet to kill and restart the container, whereas a failed readinessProbe removes the Pod's IP from Service endpoints without restarting the container.
A failed livenessProbe scales down the Deployment, while a failed readinessProbe terminates the worker node.
A failed readinessProbe restarts the container immediately, whereas a livenessProbe logs a warning in etcd.
There is no functional difference; both probes trigger identical kubelet restart policies.
assessmentQuestions.explanation: Liveness probes govern container lifecycle (restarting deadlocked or wedged processes). Readiness probes govern network visibility (removing unready pods from backing Service endpoints so traffic is never sent to containers that cannot serve requests).

assessmentQuestions.question: When configuring a multi-container Pod with InitContainers, what is the default behavior if an InitContainer exits with a non-zero code?
options: (Recommended) The Pod restarts the failing InitContainer according to the Pod's restartPolicy, and the application containers never start until all InitContainers finish with exit code 0.
The kubelet skips the failing InitContainer and starts the application containers immediately.
The Pod is permanently deleted from the cluster without notification.
The worker node enters NotReady state until manual operator intervention.
assessmentQuestions.explanation: InitContainers execute sequentially to successful completion (exit code 0). If an InitContainer fails, kubelet repeatedly restarts it according to the restartPolicy (unless Never is set), blocking application containers from initializing until preconditions are satisfied.
